reasoning: The question asks whether the Cleveland Fed's 10-year real interest rate estimate will increase between October 11 and November 10, 2026. The evidence indicates the Fed is likely to raise nominal rates by end-2026 (68-86% probability in December). However, the real interest rate depends on both nominal rates and inflation expectations. The evidence shows persistent inflation (3.4% CPI, 3% core PCE) with upward revisions to 2026-2028 inflation projections. If nominal rates rise but inflation expectations remain elevated or rise further, the real rate could remain flat or decline. The Cleveland Fed's model incorporates inflation expectations, inflation swaps, and survey data. Given that inflation is proving sticky and the Fed has revised projections upward, real rate increases are uncertain despite nominal rate hikes. The one-month forecast window is short, and monthly data updates are infrequent, limiting the probability of a measurable increase.
